newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Danish companies seek business in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Danish companies seek business in Argentina.

text.p: Envoys from a score of Danish firms will arrive in Argentina this month to explore business prospects as a part of drive to expand trade in Latin America, Danish Ambassador Leif Donde said on Friday.
"The Danish interest in Argentina is related to Mercosur and the cooperation between Mercosur and the European Union," Donde told journalists.
Mercosur is a customs union formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
The mission, to visit Argentina from September 23-25, will be headed by Danish Minister of Environment and Energy Svend Auken, who will meet President Carlos Menem and other Argentine officials.

Donde said the move was part of a Danish strategy to open new markets in countries like Mexico, Brasil, Chile and Argentina. He added that Denmark was the natural port for Argentine products to access the Baltic markets.

Many of the Danish firms are not very big, but they are well equipped and have good technology, Donde said. For instance, Denmark is the world's leading producer of windmills for electric generation and produces half of the world's machinery used in the cement industry.
The embassy has already received about 500 requests from Argentine firms willing to make business contacts.

Denmark imports from Argentina goods worth $200 million a year, mainly grain for hogs, and exports about $95 million, basically pharmaceuticals, chemicals and machinery for dairies, cement industries and meat-packing plants.
